chunks.text: I'm Emily and in today's episode we are going to learn how to speak English at the museum.
Museums are fantastic places to learn about history, art, culture and science.
If you are visiting an English speaking country, you might need to ask for information, buy a ticket, find your way around or describe exhibits in English.
So today I will teach you some useful phrases to help you feel more comfortable speaking English at the museum.
One, buying a ticket at the museum.
When you arrive at a museum, you usually need to buy a ticket.
Sometimes museums offer different types of tickets such as general admission, student discounts or tickets for special exhibitions.
Here are some useful English phrases for buying a ticket.
Common phrases at the ticket counter.
Hello, I'd like to buy a ticket please.
How much is the entrance fee?
Do you have a student discount?
Is admission free today?
What are the museum's opening hours?
Can I buy my ticket online?
Are there any special exhibitions today?
Is there a family ticket available?
Hello, I'd like to buy a ticket please.
Sure, a standard ticket is $12.
Would you like an audio guide?
Yes, please.
How much is the audio guide?
It's $5 extra.
Okay, I'll take it.
Thank you.
Tip, some museums have free admission days or discounts for students and seniors.
Don't forget to ask.
Act two, asking for directions inside the museum.
Museums can be very large with multiple floors and different sections.
If you don't know where to go, you can ask for directions.
Common phrases to ask for directions.
Excuse me, where is the art gallery?
Can you show me the way to the history section?
Where is the restroom?
Is there a cafe inside the museum?
Where can I find the gift shop?
How do I get to the second floor?
Is there an elevator?
Are there lockers to store my bag?
Excuse me, where is the dinosaur exhibit?
It's on the second floor to the left.
Thank you.
Is there an elevator?
Yes, it's right behind you.
Tip, many large museums have maps at the entrance.
You can also ask if they have a museum app to help you navigate.
Three, talking about art and exhibits.
When you see a beautiful painting or an interesting exhibit, you might want to talk about it with your friends or ask for more information.
Here are some simple phrases you can use.
Common phrases to talk about art and exhibits.
Wow, this painting is amazing.
I love the colors in this artwork.
This sculpture is very detailed.
Who is the artist?
When was this made?
What does this painting represent?
This exhibit is very interesting.
I think this painting is very peaceful.
What material is this sculpture made of?
This is my favorite artwork in the museum.
Example dialogue.
Wow, this painting is beautiful.
Yes, I love the colors.
Do you know who the artist is?
Let's check the information card.
Tip, if you're not sure how to describe art, just say, I like it.
Or it looks interesting.
Four, using an audio guide or joining a tour.
Museums often offer audio guides or guided tours to help visitors learn more about the exhibits.
Common phrases for guided tours.
Where can I get an audio guide?
How long is the tour?
Is the tour in English?
What time does the tour start?
Can I join the tour now?
Do I need to book the tour in advance?
Does the guide speak other languages?
Example dialogue.
Hello, is there an English tour today?
Yes, the next one starts at 2 p.m.
Great, how long is the tour?
It's about 45 minutes.
Tip, if you don't have time for a guided tour, you can read the information cards next to each exhibit.
Five, visiting the museum gift shop.
At the end of your visit, you might want to buy a souvenir from the gift shop.
Common phrases at the museum shop.
How much is this postcard?
Do you have any books about this artist?
Can I pay by card?
Do you have this in another size?
I'd like to buy a magnet, please.
Can I have a bag?
Do you sell posters of this painting?
Example dialogue.
Hello, how much is this museum guidebook?
Shop assistant, it's $12.
Okay, I'll take it.
Tip, museum shops often sell unique gifts related to the exhibitions.
It's a great place to buy something special.
Six, visiting the museum cafe.
If you are feeling hungry after walking around, you can visit the museum cafe.
Common phrases to use at the cafe.
Do you have a menu?
Can I have a coffee, please?
What do you recommend?
Is this seat available?
Do you have vegetarian options?
Can I get this to go?
Tip, some museums have famous cafes.
Check if they have special desserts or drinks related to the exhibitions.
That's all for today's episode.
Now you know how to buy a ticket, ask for directions, talk about exhibits, join a tour, and visit the gift shop or cafe in English.
I hope you feel more confident for your next museum visit.
